meta.title: Make Your Bed: Little Things That Can Change Your Life...And Maybe the World
meta.author: Admiral William H. McRaven

sentences: **Preface:** In 2014, I gave a **commencement speech** at my **alma mater,** the **University of Texas.**
Initially worried about my **military background,** I found students embraced my **ten lessons** from **Navy SEAL training**, which resonate with life's challenges.
People shared how small acts, like "making their bed every morning," inspired resilience.
This book expands on those lessons, incorporating stories of individuals exemplifying **discipline, perseverance,** and **courage.**

parts.title: The Importance of Small Habits in SEAL Training and Life

sentences: The **barracks** at SEAL training is a simple building near the **beach** in Coronado, California.
It has **basic** rooms with just beds and closets.
As the **day** begins, the trainees are expected to start by **making their beds** perfectly.
Instructors inspect uniforms rigorously, checking for precise **alignment** and **cleanliness**.
If standards are not met, trainees face physical **consequences** like being made into a "**sugar cookie,**" which involves getting wet and covered in sand.
Making the bed correctly is a small but important task that demonstrates **discipline** and **attention to detail**.
Throughout his **career**, the author describes how making his bed became a **constant** amidst **chaos**.
Even during major events like **9/11** and his recovery from a parachute **accident**, the act of making his bed symbolized a **return** to normalcy and a way of claiming control over his day.
In Iraq, even when sleeping on Army **cots**, the ritual of tidying his sleeping area provided a sense of **pride** and routine.

These repeated **actions** helped him and others handle the **hardships** of military life, teaching that while life can be **unpredictable**, maintaining small disciplined habits can **provide** strength and **solace**.

paragraphs.heading: Lesson from a Parachute Jump Accident
sentences: In **SEAL training**, a critical incident taught me the importance of relying on others, paralleling the lesson from the rubber raft teamwork.
During a parachute jump, I collided with another chute, resulting in chaos at 5,500 feet.
**Entangled** and partially unconscious, I finally deployed my parachute, landing far from the drop zone with severe injuries.
Recovery seemed impossible, threatening my SEAL career due to the intense physical **demands** and medical evaluations required.
Yet, crucial support from my wife, friends, and military leader **Admiral Olson** championed my return.

paragraphs.heading: Community Support in Recovery
sentences: Bedridden, self-pity was counteracted by my wife Georgeann’s tough love and care, physically aiding my wounds and mentally bolstering my spirit.
This **community of support** in various forms – emotional, physical, and professional – highlighted that no individual, even in elite SEAL groups, thrives alone.
Just as in basic SEAL training, success in overcoming life’s trials demands a reliance on others around us, underlining that the **journey of life** requires teamwork and mutual support.

parts.title: Lessons in Determination and Overcoming Unfairness

sentences: **The young midshipman** visited the SEAL training facility in Coronado with hopes of becoming a SEAL.
He met **Lieutenant Doug Huth**, who shared insights about SEAL training.
The midshipman compared himself to a frail civilian looking at photos, doubting the man could endure SEAL training.
However, he learned that this man was **Lieutenant Tom Norris**, a Medal of Honor recipient considered one of the toughest SEALs.
Norris's story exemplified that **determination outweighed physical attributes**, inspiring others to prove critics wrong.
Later, the midshipman experienced a lesson in **unfairness** during a SEAL training exercise.
Tasked with becoming a "sugar cookie" for a training rule violation, he was instructed to get wet and sandy.
This challenged his patience, as becoming a "sugar cookie" was the **instructor's arbitrary choice**—a test of resilience.

Seeking approval from **Lieutenant Phillip L. Martin**, the midshipman learned that SEAL training emphasized overcoming unfair situations, instilling the need to persevere regardless of circumstances.
Although initially, there was **hope** that Moki might **recover**, the **paralysis** from the cycling **accident** was **permanent**.
Moki displayed **remarkable resilience**, never showing **self-pity** or blaming the **accident** for his lot in life.
Instead, he became an accomplished **painter** and founded the **Super Frog Triathlon**.
Moki's story illustrates how **unfairness** in life doesn't determine your **future**.
Many **great** individuals, including Moki, are defined by how they deal with life’s **challenges** and **injustices**.

parts.title: From Adversity to Leadership and Daring Greatly

sentences: **July 1983** was a challenging time for me as I faced consequences for trying to **change my SEAL squadron**.
After being relieved of my position, my **reputation was damaged** among officers and enlisted men.
However, I had two choices: **quit** or **persevere** and prove my capability.
Opting for the latter, I took every opportunity to **outperform others** during an overseas deployment.
This dedication led me to **regain respect** and eventually, I took command of a SEAL Team and later, many SEALs.
By **2003**, I was a **one-star admiral** in combat zones, making numerous decisions that at times resulted in failure.
These failures taught me to learn, motivate myself, and face risks as a true leader.
Later, the passage transitions into a reflection on **daring greatly**.
While on a SEAL training obstacle course, I learned an essential lesson in overcoming fear by attempting the **Commando Style** for the Slide for Life.
This experience became invaluable in 2004 during a risky **daylight rescue mission** in Iraq, where **taking risks** led to success.
Throughout my career and life, understanding that **“Who Dares Wins”** taught me that living in fear of **failure** or **hardship** limits one’s potential.
Accepting and understanding **calculated risks** can reveal what is truly possible.
**Swimming** into darkness with **sharks** and overcoming **fear** is a powerful experience faced by aspiring **SEALs**.
Ensign Marc Thomas and others navigated the ocean under challenging conditions, knowing threats like the **great white shark** lurked beneath.
Despite the physical **challenges** and mental **obstacles**, their strong desire to succeed as SEALs pushed them **forward** with **courage**.
They understood that without courage, individuals and societies remain vulnerable to **bullies** and **tyrants**.
Perseverance through hardship, exemplified by American soldiers who ousted **Saddam Hussein**, serves as a lesson that strength overcomes fear, allowing for victorious resolutions.

paragraphs.heading: A Fallen Soldier's Farewell
sentences: At **Bagram Air Base**, a solemn **Ramp Ceremony** took place for a fallen **warrior**.
Soldiers lined up, forming an **honor guard** while a band played **"Amazing Grace."**
The soldier's comrades acted as **pallbearers**, carrying a **flag-draped casket** onto a waiting **C-17 aircraft**.
A **pastor recited Isaiah 6:8**, honoring the sacrifice of the fallen, in a moment filled with profound **grief and dignity**.
In these dark moments, when the **C-17** departed to **Dover Air Force Base**, the country **honored** the soldier's bravery.

Stories from **Iraq and Afghanistan** illustrated the nation's ability to **support and pride** itself on the **courage** of its **warriors**, reinforced by instances where communities united, honoring the fallen with **respect and pride**.
These moments taught the importance of holding on during life's **dark times** to find the strength to carry on.

parts.title: Never Quit: Transform the World with Simple Actions

sentences: The **commencement speech** at the University of Texas emphasizes that individuals have the **power to change** the world.
The speaker highlights the **SEAL training experience** and lessons learned there, emphasizing the importance of **never quitting**.
He shares an inspirational story of a **courageous Army Ranger**, Adam Bates, who faced immense adversity with determination, symbolizing the strength of the human spirit.
The speech underscores how **taking small actions** each day can lead to monumental change, much like making one's bed to start the day on the right note.
The speaker insists that if everyone changes the lives of **just ten people**, those changes will **ripple** through generations.
His message is clear: **taking risks**, showing **resilience**, and the determination not to give up are lessons that apply universally.
He concludes by stressing that **taking small, purposeful actions** can lead to transforming one’s life and the world at large.
The advice given is relevant to everyone, regardless of their background or situation, reminding the graduates that big change starts with simple steps like **making your bed**.
SEAL **training** teaches valuable lessons.
Despite all efforts, **uniform inspections** always found "something" wrong, leading to a "sugar-cookie" punishment.
Through this, students learned **resilience**; sometimes life just makes you a sugar cookie, and you must keep moving forward.
SEALs faced rigorous **physical events** daily, and failing to meet standards led to a "Circus," or extra calisthenics.
While **fatiguing**, **Circuses** built **strength and inner resilience**, proving failure isn’t the end but a path to growth.
If you want to **change the world**, embrace the lessons taught by **adversity** and never quit.
